audit_findings.title: SFE closing would invalidate the cash, interest-cost and share-count perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $451 million cash consideration plus approximately $21 million of RSUs; combined consideration equals 53.5% of the $883 million base equity value, and cash consideration is 3.90x the $115.68 million cash/STI balance
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would consume bridge cash, add acquisition debt and interest expense to equity-level OE, introduce RSU dilution or compensation expense, and add SFE earnings and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We have incurred, and may in the future incur, significant indebtedness in connection with acquisitions or other strategic growth initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied record describes a pending transaction expected to close during fiscal 2027 but does not demonstrate that it had closed by the valuation date. It is therefore a forward-looking perimeter change, not a demonstrated error in the as-filed valuation. Its scale would make a post-closing rerun mandatory, and the net value direction is mixed because acquired earnings must be weighed against financing costs, cash consumption, dilution and integration risk.
audit_findings.action: Confirm closing status as of September 6, 2026. Upon closing, rerun the valuation using actual consideration, cash used, financing terms, acquired debt and cash, issued or promised RSUs, transaction costs and SFE operating results.

audit_findings.title: DTA contingent consideration may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed latest fair value of €2.5 million and contractual maximum exposure of €12.0 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid earn-out is an equity-bridge liability or forecast cash outflow; omitting it overstates value attributable to common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company acquired all of the assets and assumed certain liabilities of DTA for an initial purchase price of $ 26.7 million plus potential earn-out of € 12.0 million to be paid at the end of the third year following the acquisition that is contingent upon the achievement of certain financial objectives with a maximum total purchase price of € 36.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability is demonstrated and should be represented, but it is capped at €12.0 million. That ceiling is small relative to the $766 million bear equity value, $883 million base equity value and $117 million bear-to-base scenario spread, so it cannot reasonably change the present valuation conclusion that the $37.34 market price exceeds even the $19.67 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the €2.5 million May 31, 2026 fair-value liability into the bridge and rerun after deducting it; separately sensitivity-test the €12.0 million maximum without double-counting earn-out remeasurement expense in OE.

audit_findings.title: Rabbi-trust shares may be missing from the fully diluted denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed May 31, 2026 stock-held-in-trust carrying amount is $4.860 million, but the corresponding share count and current fair value are not supplied
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted beneficiary shares would understate the fully diluted denominator and overstate value per share; alternatively, the associated deferred-compensation obligation may require bridge treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: Company common stock contributions to fund the plan are held in a rabbi trust, accounted for in a man ner similar to treasury stock and are recorded at cost in “Stock held in trust” within shareholders’ equity on the Consolidated Balance Sheets with the corresponding deferred compensation liability also recorded within shareholders’ equity on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that company shares are held in a treasury-like rabbi trust for plan participants, but it does not establish whether those shares are already included in the 51.92154 million denominator. The carrying amount cannot reliably be converted into a share count because it is recorded at cost rather than current market value. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the May 31 or September 6, 2026 rabbi-trust share count and reconcile it share-by-share to cover-page shares, the 657,723 award inventory and the valuation denominator; rerun per-share values for any omitted economic claims.

audit_findings.title: Retained divestiture liabilities may fall outside continuing-operations OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed discontinued-operations cash outflow was $2.697 million in FY2024 and nil in FY2025, but current reserves, indemnity limits and expected payments are not separately disclosed
audit_findings.mechanism: Future payments for retained liabilities or indemnities would reduce equity cash flows or require a non-operating liability deduction from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: All discontinued operations activity included within the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Earnings and the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the periods presented relate to impacts from certain retained liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: Historical retained-liability effects are demonstrated, but the supplied filings do not quantify the remaining reserve, maximum indemnity exposure or expected payment schedule. The absence of FY2025 discontinued-operations cash flow does not establish that the obligations have expired. The possible valuation effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile retained divestiture reserves within other current and long-term liabilities, obtain indemnity caps and expected payment schedules, and either deduct the present obligation in the bridge or include the payments explicitly in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 income contains a nonrecurring LIFO liquidation benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $3.7 million pretax; computed approximately $2.842 million after tax using the 23.2% FY2025 effective rate, equal to 5.2% of the $54.6 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If unadjusted, the benefit raises FY2025 OE and the fitted historical trend used to set anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended August 31, 2025, the Company experienced a liquidation of LIFO inventory layers, which resulted in a decrease in cost of goods sold and a corresponding increase in pre-tax income of approximately $ 3.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The nonrecurring benefit is demonstrated. Even treating the entire estimated after-tax amount as a direct anchor overstatement—more severe than its likely effect through a ten-year trend—would reduce rather than increase value and would not close the gap between the $37.34 price and the $19.67 bull value. It therefore cannot change the present investment conclusion, although normalization improves estimate quality.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $3.7 million pretax benefit was removed; if not, tax-effect it consistently, refit the ten-year log trend and refresh all scenario values.

audit_findings.title: The latest OE includes tax benefits explicitly described as nonrepeatable
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filing separately identifies a $0.620 million decrease in unrecognized tax benefits from statute-of-limitations lapses, but does not quantify the complete stock-compensation and nonrepeatable tax-planning benefits
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring tax benefits raise after-tax OE and can raise both the latest observation and the fitted anchor used throughout the valuation.
audit_findings.evidence: The fiscal 2025 effective tax rate was slightly higher than the statutory 21% primarily as a result of state income taxes and taxes in foreign jurisdictions with rates higher than the U.S. which were partially offset by one-time tax benefits related to the lapse of the statute of limitations on uncertain tax positions, tax benefits related to stock compensation, and global tax planning initiatives that will not repeat in future periods due to certain tax attributes that are no longer available.
audit_findings.explanation: Management explicitly identifies nonrepeatable benefits, so this is not merely hypothetical. However, the supplied rate reconciliation does not isolate the aggregate benefit attributable to all three cited sources, preventing a reliable normalized tax rate or valuation impact from being calculated. The known $0.620 million lapse component is small, but it is insufficient to establish the materiality of the total adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the dollar tax benefit from each statute lapse, stock-compensation item and expiring tax-planning attribute; recalculate FY2025 OE at a sustainable jurisdictional tax rate, refit the anchor and rerun all scenarios.
